newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- South Korea's trade deficit amounted to $5.49 billion in the first two months of 1997, up 47.5 percent from the $3.72 billion recorded in the same 1996 span.
- Koh Kun to be named new Prime Minister, government sources said. President Kim Young-sam is also expected to announce a new cabinet lineup tomorrow.

- The first half of the year will see a decrease in the employment rate of university graduates. According to research by Maeil Business Newspaper, the LG Group, Hanwha Group, and Sunkyong Group are planning to cut their employment plans.
- The Labour Ministery said employment in the manufacturing sector fell by 5,000 jobs from 1992.
- The listing of Korea Telecom shares on the Korea Stock Exchange will be postponed, a Ministery of Fiance and Economy official said.

- Dongbu Group will enter the semiconductor business. It will enter into technical joint venture with foreign companies, including IBM, to gain technical know-how. It plans to begin manufacturing 256 megabit DRAM by 1999.
